content:
In recent years, Macs have become increasingly affordable. With lower starting prices, more memory and storage per dollar, and the launch of the MacBook Neo, Apple is truly becoming one of the best-value options on the market for the first time.

Unfortunately, Apple has hiked prices significantly due to the ongoing memory shortage. Macs aren't quite the bargain they were a few weeks ago, but there are still some excellent deals out there—and if you need a new computer, I'd still argue that Macs represent a strong value proposition compared to the rest of the computer market right now.

MacBook Air

Until the MacBook Neo launched, the MacBook Air was the entry point to Apple's laptop lineup. While the MacBook Neo's arrival makes its value proposition a little awkward, if you want a slightly better experience and don't need anything particularly fancy, I think the MacBook Air is still a great laptop.

MagSafe, a P3 wide colour gamut display, Center Stage for the camera, and longer battery life are just a few of the highlights of the MacBook Air. It's also available in a 15-inch version, which the MacBook Neo is not.

Here are the deals available across the entire MacBook Air line right now:

MacBook Neo

Not much explanation needed for this one—the MacBook Neo is Apple's first affordable MacBook, starting at just $699.

There are definitely some trade-offs compared to the MacBook Air mentioned above, but for the price, it's an exceptional value. The build quality, display resolution, and macOS experience are essentially uncompromised. Sure, you'll have to accept a slower A18 Pro chip (but honestly, the performance isn't bad at all), fewer ports, and only 8GB of memory, but that's entirely reasonable at this price point. It also comes in some delightful colours like citrus yellow, coral pink, and indigo.

The MacBook Neo doesn't see many discounts at major retailers right now, but Apple does sell refurbished models for $100 to $120 less than retail. Apple's refurbished units come with the same one-year warranty, are like-new condition, have all major components replaced, and won't have any scratches or degraded battery life.

  • MacBook Neo: 256GB storage, 8GB memory – $689 at Amazon ($10 off)
  • MacBook Neo: 512GB storage, 8GB memory, Touch ID – $789 at Amazon ($10 off)
  • Refurbished MacBook Neo: 256GB storage, 8GB memory – $599 at Apple Store
  • Refurbished MacBook Neo: 512GB storage, 8GB memory, Touch ID – $679 at Apple Store

MacBook Pro

At the top of the lineup is the MacBook Pro. You'll get the absolute best specs, but with an important caveat. Reports suggest Apple will be redesigning the high-end MacBook Pro later this year with OLED, a touchscreen, and a thinner body.

However, that new design will only debut on models with M5 Pro and M5 Max chips—so if you're buying a base model with the M5 chip, there's absolutely no problem picking one up now. It's also a good choice if you couldn't care less about that new design, since M5 Pro and M5 Max are already incredibly powerful new chips.
